overall: On reconsideration, the AG reissued OML 2024-135 and found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by omitting the secrecy statute from its Purpose 7 notice, because citing it would have compromised the executive session's purpose; it also directed revision of the draft minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the December 11, 2023 executive session, citing only Purpose 7 without the governing law, was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it did not cite to the law requiring secrecy where doing so would have compromised the purpose for the December 11 executive session.

allegations.summary: On the AG's own in camera review of draft December 11, 2023 executive session minutes, the AG found they did not summarize discussions as the law requires.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we note that the draft minutes provided to our office do not contain the level of detail required to comply with the Open Meeting Law where they do not summarize the discussions held during the almost hour-long meeting.

allegations.summary: The AG's original concern that the executive session discussion may not have been proper was withdrawn on reconsideration.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, we no longer have concerns about the propriety of the discussion held in executive session on December 11, 2023.

remedy: The Board should revise the minutes in accordance with this guidance before approving the minutes.
remedy_passage: The Board should revise the minutes in accordance with this guidance before approving the minutes.
